## PREVENTION OF BACTERIAL INFECTIONS IN A PATIENT WITH MALIGNANCY
Antimicrobial prophylaxis is often given to patients likely to have profound,
prolonged neutropenia. Profound neutropenia is less than 100 neutrophils and
bands per microliter, and such neutropenia is considered prolonged when it is
expected to last more than 7 days. Most patients who should receive prophylaxis
have received stem cell transplants or are undergoing induction chemotherapy for
acute leukemia.
## If antibacterial prophylaxis is indicated
Duration of therapy: During period of expected neutropenia
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO q12h ($) [R,DI] < OR >
Levofloxacin 500 mg PO q24h ($) [R]
< OR >
Trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole 1 DS tablet PO q12h ($) [R,DI] < OR >
Cefpodoxime 100 mg PO q12h ($$) [R]
